hn-50257325.t: AI promised less work. I've never worked more
hn-50257325.s: Agents made implementation cheap, so I started doing far more of it in parallel. My GitHub history since 2019 shows what that did: as VP of Technology I am back at my full-stack engineer pace, with…
ex: The pitch was that AI would give us our time back. Write less boilerplate, delegate the boring parts, go home earlier. I am not complaining about the tools. I use agents for all of my engineering work now, and I wrote about how that setup evolved and why I still read the code. I can investigate and ship things that would not have been worth starting two years ago. But somewhere this year I noticed that I am working more than I ever have, and that it feels heavier than it used to. Not because any single task is harder. Because there are so many more of them, all at once. This post is me trying to understand that, with some data from my own GitHub history. As a full-stack engineer, a normal week for me meant two or three serious tasks. A feature, a tricky bug, maybe a migration. Each one needed real focus, but I could hold one of them in my head at a time, finish it, and move to the next. Today my week looks completely different.

hn-50260814.t: Anthropic trained Claude on illegally obtained Stanford professors' books
hn-50260814.s: The AI company pirated at least 10 Stanford academics’ work in a $1.5 billion copyright settlement.
ex: AI giant Anthropic illegally scraped and pirated the work of over 10 Stanford professors to train its Claude models, a federal judge ruled in a May 2026 lawsuit. Anthropic previously trained Claude on illegally obtained texts from professors Tobias Wolff, Abraham Verghese, Chang-Rae Lee, Daniel Mason, Hayagreeva Rao and Myra Strober. In Bartz v. Anthropic, which the Authors Alliance calls the largest copyright settlement involving an AI company, Judge William Alsup ruled that Anthropic could no longer pirate books to create a permanent central library. While blocking the piracy of work to train AI, Alsup justified the legal acquisition of books to train Claude’s Large Language Models (LLMs) as fair use. He compared AI training to how humans can read, internalize and remember a book’s themes and style.

hn-50257326.s: AI-generated text is harder to spot, but that hasn’t deterred them
ex: AI-generated text is harder to spot, but that hasn’t deterred them Eliza Strickland is IEEE Spectrum's features editor. She also covers AI and biomedical engineering. Ellia Lebleu is a cofounder of the WikiProject AI Cleanup effort to keep Wikipedia human-written. Ellia Lebleu is a founding member of the WikiProject AI Cleanup, a volunteer effort launched in 2023 to find and remove AI-generated material from Wikipedia that breaks the website’s guidelines. When the cleanup began, AI writing was often betrayed by conspicuous clichés. Today, the project’s volunteers are developing tools to detect subtler forms of machine-generated content and debating AI’s role in the world’s most widely used encyclopedia. When did you realize Wikipedia had a problem with AI-generated material? Ellia Lebleu: It was around December 2023. A few other editors and I were chatting on Wikipedia’s Discord server, and we had all seen very strange articles with the same odd characteristics.

hn-50261589.t: Amazon Is Gutting Its AI Division After Sustained Failure
hn-50261589.s: Amazon is gutting its AI labs and funneling its resources into a new project headed by a noted AI robotics guru.
ex: Not a whole lot, it turns out. Unlike its competitors in the tech megacorp scene, Amazon’s standout AI model — organized under the name “Nova” — is about the farthest thing from a household name. And that’s not likely to change anytime soon, because the ecommerce giant is now gutting its in-house AI labs, Bloomberg reports. Per the outlet, Amazon is scaling back the ambitions of most of its Nova AI models and reorganizing its AI development teams as part of an effort to narrow its focus on “highest priority” goals, after its power-hungry large language models turned out to be a bust. Accordingly, the company has put most of its AI models on ice, Amazon insiders told Bloomberg. This includes its text-based Nova models, as well as video- and image-generating models, all of which have been placed in a state of “keep the lights on,” meaning they’re technically still supported, but only receive the bare minimum resources needed to sustain them.

hn-50261647.t: Classification of Finite Simple Groups Formalized in Lean
hn-50261647.s: A complete formalization in Lean of the first-generation proof of the classification of finite simple groups, with every logical step checked by Lean’s kernel.
ex: A new group theory result that came out of this formalization project is reported in this paper. While formalizing the first-generation proof, we found counterexamples to a closure assertion used in a published route to the Unbalanced Group Theorem. The paper explains the obstruction and gives an alternative argument for the simple-group case, built on Solomon’s 1976 theory of maximal 2-components, whose key step is Theorem 2.3, the preservation of simple tops. We are working with group theorists to compile the errata we found in the literature, and will publish them here. The classification of finite simple groups is one of the great collective achievements of mathematics. Its first-generation proof spans thousands of journal pages, written by about a hundred mathematicians over several decades. It shows that every finite simple group is cyclic of prime order, alternating, of Lie type, or one of 26 sporadic groups.

hn-50255298.t: The Mythical Man-Month in the Age of AI
hn-50255298.s: An update to Brooks's Law in the age of AI.
ex: Last weekend I watched four people desperately trying to get a laptop to connect to a screen. I was happily observing their efforts, with zero intent to join in. My reply: "Haha sorry no! My experience is that adding more people will not solve this problem any quicker". "Adding manpower to a late software project makes it later." It was formulated by computer scientist Frederick P. Brooks Jr. in his 1975 book The Mythical Man-Month, based on his experience managing the IBM OS/360 project. However I got to thinking. Does this still hold up in the age of AI agents and LLMs? At first glance, you’d think no. The traditional bottlenecks -- onboarding time, endless stand-ups, and office politics -- disappear overnight. An AI agent is up to speed in milliseconds and doesn't demand a coffee break. But when you look closer, and the law hasn't vanished. It just mutated. The famous "Baby Problem" remains: nine agents still can’t deliver a baby in one month. Sequential tasks are still sequential.

ex: A fast reasoning model served by several independent providers. AllModels keeps text routes in the fallback pool and sends image requests only to a provider that can actually read them. AllModels continuously brings new abliterated models and competitive inference providers into one routing layer. Get the latest models, provider diversity, and capacity failover through a single security-hardened API—without rebuilding your integration each time the market moves. Use messages, streaming, function tools, and the familiar OpenAI chat schema. Use input items, streaming events, reasoning controls, structured output, custom tools, and hosted web search.

hn-50258868.t: Here be monsters: What do you still need to know when agents do the work?
hn-50258868.s: AI agents write code faster than anyone can read it. What engineers still need: fundamentals, breadth, and the willingness to dive in when it breaks.
ex: CI was failing. This was unexpected. I have dialed in my agentic workflow to a point where I would be surprised if one of my agents committed a branch that had failing tests. Maybe it's a CI flake or environment issue? Wait, it's SonarQube complaining about App.tsx? Did we pull in a new suspicious dependency from npm or something? Nope. SonarQube is flagging this file for cyclomatic complexity. Haven't seen that one in a while. Yep. App.tsx consists of about 30 lines of code, except 15 of those lines are actually entire components that Codex decided to write each on a single line. That itself would be ok, just run it through prettier and we're done. But that doesn't explain the cyclomatic complexity. Each of these was a fairly involved component with a good amount of display and business logic. Old self would have carefully refactored it and made sure the code was readable.

hn-50260960.t: Data Recovery CEO Indicted for Allegedly Scamming Ransomware Victims
hn-50260960.s: A federal grand jury indicted MonsterCloud CEO Zohar Pinhasi last month for allegedly defrauding clients of his ransomware data recovery business, which was the subject of a 2019 ProPublica…
ex: ProPublica is a nonprofit, investigative newsroom that exposes corruption. We report in all 50 states and partner with local newsrooms. Our work spurs real-world impact and has received numerous awards, including nine Pulitzer Prizes. How Recent Arrivals at the Border Have Changed the Country and Its Attitudes SCOTUS Justices’ Beneficial Relationships With Billionaire Donors A Florida man who was the subject of a 2019 investigation by ProPublica was indicted last month on federal charges that he defrauded clients of his ransomware data recovery firm. According to the Justice Department, the man, Zohar Pinhasi, told customers he could recover their encrypted files without having to pay hackers, when, in reality, he paid the ransom and charged victims a hefty fee on top. The indictment mirrors the findings from ProPublica’s 2019 article “The Trade Secret,” which centered on Pinhasi and his scheme.

hn-50261319.s: Genie 4 introduces real-time interactive world simulation with native audio, advanced physics, natural human motion, and steering powered by Gemini models.
ex: Today, we are announcing Genie 4, our new world model, which unlocks unprecedented realism and improves real-time interactive simulation. Genie 4 is natively multimodal, enabling audio-like music, ambient noises, and interactive dialogue to be simultaneously generated with the world. The Genie 4 model incorporates and builds on capabilities from the Gemini family: Gemini Omni anchors the simulations in real-world appearance and behavior, while other Gemini models provide the complex reasoning needed to help maintain a simulation’s coherence and continuity. With this foundation, you can set an event in motion, and Genie 4 simulates what happens next: how the world responds, how it sounds, and how the people in it move, react, and speak. Understanding and simulating the world is a crucial aspect of building AGI.

hn-50259604.t: US Government is hiding a secret court ruling about how it spies on Americans
hn-50259604.s: Two US senators say the Trump administration is breaking the law by withholding the FISA court decision while it presses Congress to renew America’s most sweeping surveillance program.
ex: Two Democratic senators who have long overseen US intelligence say the Trump administration is illegally withholding a secret court’s findings from Congress until lawmakers renew a program that lets federal agents read Americans’ communications without a warrant. Seven months ago, the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Court objected to search filters that let intelligence analysts pull Americans’ messages from intercepted data without the approvals, written justifications, or records the law requires. The court approved another year of surveillance anyway. The ruling has never been made public, and Senators Ron Wyden of Oregon and Adam Schiff of California say the administration’s own deadline for releasing it passed in September. The program, Section 702 of the Foreign Intelligence Surveillance Act (FISA), lapsed in June after Congress failed to renew it, though collection continues under the court’s March approval.

hn-50263854.t: Discord will soon let anyone find public server messages through Google
hn-50263854.s: Starting on November 16, 2026, conversations in Discoverable Servers will be easier to find for people searching the web. Admins can choose which channels are surfaced on the web.
ex: Discoverable Servers are the most public spaces on Discord, with at least 1,000 members. Their admins chose to list them in Server Discovery so anyone can join them, no invite link needed. Discussions in Discoverable Servers will soon be easier to find when you search the web, so you can find the answer you’re looking for and step straight into the conversation on Discord. Admins and members can decide if and how their content is shared, and those controls start rolling out today, ahead of any changes. Over the years, Discord has built different kinds of spaces, so every group can decide how big the party gets and who can find it: Today, there are more than 63,000 Discoverable Servers, spanning communities from speedrunning to language learning to niche corners of every fandom. People find their way into communities they'd never have stumbled across otherwise. Until now, that's all being Discoverable meant. Server Discovery was built for finding servers, not answers.

ex: One photo + one sentence → a finished talking-head video with a digital human. Script, lip-synced AI presenter, voice clean-up, captions, and pro-YouTuber-style packaging — fully automated by your AI agent. Click a GIF (or "Watch") to play the full video. Every demo below was produced with this repo. - Digital human from one photo — a fixed presenter (face, outfit, voice description, prompt template) stored in persona.json, so every video is the same person. Composite her into any scene (livestream studio, shop, classroom, Kyoto street) with GPT Image first, then make her talk. - Lip-synced talking clips — the script is split into ≤ 15-second segments and generated with Grok Video 1.5 through Renoise MCP. Other models (Wan 3.0, OmniHuman for your own recording) are documented. - Cost gate — the agent always quotes segments · seconds · credits · balance first and waits for your "yes". It generates segment 1 for you to check before batching the rest.

gh-1435425970.s: Motion capture for any creature from one AI video: two cameras in one frame, a DINOv2 joint reader, the rig fitted in both views, a GLB out.
ex: @patchgg · dragon, giant spider, fire demon, wolf · one AI clip per move, $0.26 each, read and fitted in under a minute. anymove turns one AI video into an animation for any rigged creature, wings, tails and eight legs included. A video model films the creature from two cameras in one frame, front on the left and side on the right. A joint reader trained on that one creature finds every joint in both views. A joint sits at the same height in both, so the pair pins it in 3D, and the rig is fitted to those joints frame by frame and exported as a GLB. The method is @CanItCode's; the MiniMax H3 LoRA step is @Graalitoo's idea. This repo is our working version of both, with the agent skills to run it. You need an NVIDIA GPU with CUDA (24 GB to train a reader; reading and fitting need much less), Python 3.11, Blender 5.x on your PATH (or BLENDER=/path/to/blender), and a fal key to make new clips. Fit the dragon's roar on the CPU, no Blender or downloads needed.
